decision_a.overall_risk_rationale: Occupancy and revenue metrics are strong and improving, but average guest rating has fallen (~-5.9%) while volume of reviews increased. Multiple recent reviews point to recurring operational/guest-experience issues (noise, very small rooms/limited in‑room facilities, breakfast crowding and unclear extra charges) that could further depress satisfaction and future demand if not addressed.
decision_a.executive_summary: Solar dos Poetas benefits from an excellent central location, friendly staff and strong occupancy / revenue performance. Recent guest feedback during the decision window repeatedly highlights problems with street/corridor noise and poor soundproofing, small room layout and limited in-room amenities, breakfast timing/crowding and unclear ancillary charges/payments. Priorities should focus on: (1) mitigating noise and setting accurate expectations, (2) addressing small-room amenity and storage shortcomings, (3) improving breakfast service hours and transparency about luggage/fees and payment methods, and (4) checking elevator reliability and accessibility. Combine immediate operational fixes and clearer communication with medium-term capital and process investments where needed.

priorities.area: Noise and soundproofing / room location expectations
priorities.problem: Multiple recent reviews report significant noise from the square (live music), trams and corridor (doors slamming, people), and poor soundproofing leading to disturbed sleep and lower satisfaction.
priorities.recommended_action: Immediate: provide complimentary earplugs, offer white-noise machines or mobile app suggestions at check-in, proactively reassign particularly noise-sensitive guests to quieter rooms where possible, and add a late-night contact for noise complaints. Short term: update room descriptions and booking channels to clearly communicate which rooms face the square and potential noise. Medium term: commission an audit of windows/doors and prioritize installation of improved seals/double glazing or corridor sound mitigation where cost-effective.
priorities.rationale: Quick operational steps reduce immediate guest disturbance and limit negative reviews while medium-term investments will reduce recurrence. Accurate online descriptions reduce guest dissatisfaction from mismatched expectations.
supporting_evidence: “Room completely non-soundproof. You can hear both the noises from the square in front of the hotel (nightlife) and people in the corridor…”

priorities.area: Room size, layout and basic in‑room amenities
priorities.problem: Guests frequently report rooms that feel very small with inadequate storage, small bathrooms with constrained layouts and missing basic amenities (no kettle/coffee). This reduces comfort, especially for travellers with luggage.
priorities.recommended_action: Operational: provide simple in-room amenities on request (kettle/coffee kit), add hooks/shelves or modular storage solutions in rooms where feasible, and offer luggage-handling assistance or temporary in-room luggage stands. Update room descriptions and photos to reflect actual room size/layout so guest expectations align. Medium term: review whether some rooms can be reconfigured to improve storage/flow (capital assessment).
priorities.rationale: Simple amenity additions and small fixture changes can significantly improve perceived value at low cost; accurate descriptions reduce future mismatch complaints.
supporting_evidence: “Rooms really small… Bathroom was so small in order to sit on the loo we had to have the shower door open. Facilities in room very limited. No space for cupboard… No kettle/coffee machine etc.”

priorities.area: Breakfast capacity/hours and ancillary charges / payment methods
priorities.problem: Guests praised breakfast quality but report crowded dining room and that breakfast start time is too late for some (requests for 7:00). Several guests also reported surprise and dissatisfaction with a charge for luggage storage and at least one guest noted inability to pay by credit card.
priorities.recommended_action: Immediate: review and publish breakfast hours and consider opening earlier (e.g., 7:00) if operationally feasible; implement crowd-management measures (staggered seating, signage, add temporary staff at peak times). Clarify and publish luggage-storage policy and fees at booking and check-in; consider waiving the fee or offering a clear, value‑based fee. Ensure payment options are clearly listed on the website and at reception and resolve any card-payment limitations as a priority.
priorities.rationale: Breakfast is a frequently-cited strength; reducing crowding and matching hours to guest needs will protect satisfaction. Clear communication on fees and payment methods prevents surprise charges and related negative sentiment.
supporting_evidence: “Breakfast was excellent… A little bit crowded in the morning… ”
“It would have been great if the breakfast start time was earlier, say 7am”
“It's the first time I've been asked to pay a fee for luggage storage, and it was quite expensive… If it had been clear from the start, I would have chosen another hotel.”

priorities.problem: At least one recent review mentions an inconvenience associated with the elevator; combined with small rooms and high floors this may affect guest convenience and accessibility.
priorities.recommended_action: Inspect elevator performance and maintenance records; address any reliability issues promptly. Provide clear signage about elevator use and offer staff assistance for guests with mobility issues or heavy luggage. If capacity is limited, adjust room allocation (avoid booking guests with accessibility needs into upper floors without assistance).
priorities.rationale: Maintaining a reliable elevator service supports guest comfort and prevents negative experiences related to carrying luggage or mobility limitations.

limitations: Only 20 of 140 reviews from the decision window were provided for detailed review; conclusions are therefore based on a sample of recent reviews and may not reflect the full distribution of guest feedback.
No room-type-level performance, inventory or layout details were supplied (cannot quantify how many rooms face the square vs courtyard or which floors are affected).
No operational cost, staffing rosters or maintenance records were provided; recommendations involving capital works or staffing changes require internal feasibility and cost assessment.
No data on payment systems or the specific cause of the reported inability to pay by card; verification with front-desk/payment provider needed before action.

decision_b.overall_risk_rationale: Business performance (RevPAR/REVPor/TrevPAR) is improving, but customer sentiment and average rating are declining while the expectation–experience gap and semantic misalignment are rising. Several operational/structural experience issues (bathroom layout/amenities, room comfort/noise, breakfast replenishment, and a surprise baggage charge/payment clarity) are producing expectation violations and emerging negative mentions; these warrant prioritized managerial attention but do not indicate an immediate systemic safety crisis.
decision_b.executive_summary: Preserve clear strengths (location and staff). Address a small set of evidence-backed friction points: (1) bathroom condition and in-room amenities (multiple complaints and expectation violations), (2) room comfort and noise (recurring guest reports of very small rooms and poor soundproofing), (3) breakfast service friction (generally positive but repeated complaints about replenishment, crowding and hours), (4) booking/payment clarity and baggage-deposit policy (expectation violation/emerging negative), and (5) monitor sentiment / expectation gap metrics (rising gap and falling sentiment). Recommend targeted operational/process reviews, guest-facing communication updates, and assessments where the scope is unclear before any capital investment.

priorities.problem: Multiple reviews describe small, awkwardly configured bathrooms and missing expected amenities (no kettle, cramped toilets) that violate guest expectations given price/description.
priorities.recommended_action: Commission a focused rooms/maintenance assessment to (a) verify typical bathroom layouts across room types, (b) identify low-cost in-room amenity fixes (e.g., provision/placement of kettles/coffee facilities if appropriate), and (c) review room descriptions/photos to ensure they accurately represent bathroom size/arrangement. If assessment finds structural constraints, prepare a medium-term plan (scope/cost estimate) for remedial measures or clearer rate/room-type communication.
priorities.rationale: Evidence shows a net-negative pattern (9 mentions, 7 negative) with an expectation violation and emerging negative signal specifically about bathroom setup and amenities. Multiple guests explicitly said the bathroom was too small or awkward, and that room facilities were limited (no kettle), creating disappointment and statements that the room was not value-appropriate.

priorities.problem: Repeated guest complaints about very small rooms (limited storage/space) and significant nighttime and street noise (market/singers, trams, cars) that harm sleep and perceived comfort.
priorities.recommended_action: Perform an operational review to (a) identify room types/floors most affected by external noise and small layouts, (b) update booking content to set accurate expectations for room size and view (e.g., courtyard shaft vs. city view), and (c) implement near-term operational mitigations (e.g., guest communication at check-in about noise, offer earplugs, preferential assignment when possible). Commission an acoustics/maintenance inspection if many guests report noise to evaluate whether targeted soundproofing is feasible/cost-effective.

priorities.problem: Although breakfast is frequently praised, multiple guests report insufficient variety/replenishment, crowding/wait times for tables, and hours that do not accommodate some early departures.
priorities.recommended_action: Conduct an operational review of breakfast service: evaluate buffet replenishment processes and timing, table turnover/seat availability (flow during peak times), and current breakfast start time vs. guest needs. Consider minor operational changes (replenishment protocol, clearer signage for service hours, queue management) and test adjustments. Preserve aspects guests value (quality, variety for most).
priorities.rationale: Breakfast is a clear strength (63 mentions, 55 positive), but it shows emerging negative signals and an expectation violation: guests specifically cite delayed or inadequate buffet replenishment, difficulty finding a free table, and start time limitations.

priorities.problem: Guests report unexpected baggage-storage fees and an unclear payment/room description (e.g., bathroom/room description), constituting an expectation violation and a reputational friction.
priorities.recommended_action: Review and, if needed, update booking content and pre-arrival communication to ensure payment methods, any luggage-deposit fees, and room descriptions (bathroom/size/view) are explicit. Evaluate the baggage-deposit policy and whether it should be changed or simply better communicated; ensure front desk procedures transparently record and communicate any charge before accepting luggage.
priorities.rationale: Although the count of mentions is small (booking/payment: 1 negative mention), it explicitly flags an expectation violation and is an emerging negative topic. Surprises about charges ("first time I've been asked to pay a fee for luggage storage") create disproportionate guest dissatisfaction relative to frequency and are easy to address via clearer communication or policy review.

priorities.area: Monitor: sentiment / expectation–experience gap and semantic misalignment
priorities.problem: Average sentiment and average rating are decreasing while expectation–experience gap and semantic misalignment metrics are rising; without corrective action on the specific experience frictions identified above, these trends could broaden.
priorities.recommended_action: Track sentiment, average rating, expectation–experience gap, high-misalignment share and percent negative reviews weekly. After implementing the above interventions, monitor whether these metrics stabilize or reverse. If declines continue despite operational fixes, escalate to a broader experience review.
priorities.rationale: Experience indicators show a moderate increase in EXPECTATION_EXPERIENCE_GAP_AVG (0.0406 -> 0.11) and SEMANTIC_MISALIGNMENT_SCORE_AVG (0.0312 -> 0.1175), while SENTIMENT_SCORE_AVG and AVG_RATING are trending down. These are system-level warning signals that justify monitoring and follow-up after targeted interventions.
supporting_evidence: Experience indicators: EXPECTATION_EXPERIENCE_GAP_AVG increased from 0.0406 to 0.11; SEMANTIC_MISALIGNMENT_SCORE_AVG increased from 0.0312 to 0.1175.
Preliminary signals: 'increasing_expectation_gap' (severity: high) and 'increasing_misalignment' (severity: high); 'declining_sentiment' (severity: medium).
Business performance: RevPAR and revenue metrics increasing while sentiment and ratings fall (supports need to monitor experience even during good revenue performance).

limitations: Selected complaints are diagnostic and not statistically representative of the entire review population; prevalence should be assessed using full-window metadata.

Some issues (e.g., room size, building layout, soundproofing) may be structural; the evidence does not determine scope, cost, or technical feasibility of capital fixes—assessment is recommended before investment decisions.
Booking/payment evidence is based on a small number of mentions but represents a high-impact expectation violation; confirm prevalence before making policy changes.
Sentiment and expectation-gap metrics are aggregated signals; they indicate direction but do not by themselves identify root cause without the targeted reviews and assessments recommended above.
